1.title: Resource Drift, Refresh-Only, moved and removed Blocks
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Resource Drift, Refresh-Only, moved and removed Blocks. It covers the exam area six. Terraform state management. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. What drift is. Refresh-only mode. Refactoring without destroying: the moved block. Removing from state without destroying: the removed block. Other state tools in this objective. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: six. Terraform state management. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What drift is
1.text: What drift is. Drift is a difference between the real infrastructure and what Terraform's state and configuration say. It happens when someone changes a resource outside Terraform (a console edit, another tool, an automatic process).

1.title: What drift is, continued
1.text: What drift is. The figure shows this: Drift: reality changes outside Terraform, then plan finds the difference.

1.title: What drift is, continued
1.text: What drift is. A setting was changed outside Terraform. Refreshes the state, sees the difference and proposes to change it back to match the configuration. A resource was deleted outside Terraform. Proposes to create it again. A new resource appeared outside Terraform. Ignores it: Terraform only manages what it created or imported. Exam tip: Drift is found during plan (and apply ) because Terraform refreshes the state first. The default fix is to apply the configuration, which overwrites the outside change.

1.title: Refresh-only mode
1.text: Refresh-only mode. You may want to accept the real values into the state without changing the infrastructure. Use refresh-only mode. terraform plan -refresh only. Shows how the state would change to match reality; no infrastructure change. terraform apply -refresh only. Updates the state (after approval) to match reality. terraform refresh. Older shortcut for the same, deprecated because it does not ask for approval. After a refresh-only apply, update the configuration if you also want the new values to be the desired state; otherwise the next normal plan will change them back. Exam tip: -refresh only updates only the state. It never changes real infrastructure. terraform refresh is deprecated in favor of apply -refresh only.

1.title: Refactoring without destroying: the moved block
1.text: Refactoring without destroying: the moved block. When you rename a resource or move it into a module, Terraform would normally destroy the old address and create the new one. A moved block tells Terraform that the object is the same and updates the state address instead. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Refactoring without destroying: the moved block, continued
1.text: Refactoring without destroying: the moved block. Purpose. Rename or relocate a resource or module without recreating it. Keep it? Keep it long enough for everyone to apply, then it may be removed. Alternative. terraform state mv (a manual, one-time C L I change).

1.title: Removing from state without destroying: the removed block
1.text: Removing from state without destroying: the removed block. A removed block stops managing a resource without destroying the real object. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Removing from state without destroying: the removed block, continued
1.text: Removing from state without destroying: the removed block. destroy false. Remove from state, keep the real object. destroy true (the default if the block is just deleted). The object is destroyed. The C L I alternative is terraform state rm A D D R E S S. Exam tip: moved renames without recreating. removed with destroy false forgets without destroying. Deleting a resource block normally destroys the real object.

1.title: Other state tools in this objective
1.text: Other state tools in this objective. terraform apply -replace A D D R E S S. Recreate a resource that is broken. terraform state mv or rm. Manual address changes and removal. Drift detection in H C P Terraform. Scheduled health assessments that report drift (Module sixteen).

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Someone changed an instance's tags in the console. What does the next terraform plan show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A change to update the tags back to the configuration. Plan refreshes the state, finds the difference and proposes to restore the configured values.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants to accept the real values into the state without touching any infrastructure. What should they run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: terraform apply -refresh-only. Refresh-only apply updates the state to match reality and changes no infrastructure.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A resource block is renamed from web to application. How can Terraform avoid destroying and recreating it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Add a moved block with from and to. A moved block tells Terraform the object is the same and updates its address in the state.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants Terraform to stop managing a resource but leave the real object running. What should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A removed block with destroy set to false. A removed block with destroy equals false removes the object from state and keeps the real resource.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which command is deprecated because it updates state without asking for approval? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: terraform refresh. terraform refresh is deprecated; use apply with the refresh-only option.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A new resource was created manually outside Terraform and is not in the configuration. What does plan do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It ignores the resource. Terraform manages only what it created or imported, so it ignores unmanaged objects.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is drift? Answer: Real infrastructure differing from the state and configuration. Question two. When does Terraform detect drift? Answer: During plan and apply, when it refreshes the state. Question three. What does refresh-only change? Answer: Only the state.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does a moved block do? Answer: Renames or relocates an object without recreating it. Question five. What does destroy equals false in a removed block do? Answer: Removes from state and keeps the real object. Question six. What is the C L I command to remove from state? Answer: terraform state rm.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Drift: outside changes; found by plan; apply restores the configuration. Refresh-only: plan or apply -refresh-only updates state only; terraform refresh deprecated. moved: rename or move without recreating. removed: destroy equals false forgets without destroying; state rm is the C L I way.
